value.reason: server.ts:185 calls app.use(cors()) with no options. With no origin setting, the cors middleware sends Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * on every route. The policy is global, so it covers endpoints that return Profile-category data to the public. These include /rest/memories (getMemories), /rest/products/:id/reviews, /rest/user/authentication-details and the /api/${name}s REST resources that finale builds automatically from models. Some of those resources send model attributes back except for a configured exclude list. That matches the positive example, where a bare cors() sits in front of a route returning records that include user data. The negative example differs only by limiting the origin, and this code has no such limit. So any untrusted website can make cross-origin requests to these APIs and read the responses. This is a permissive cross-domain policy, and it falls short of the reasonable security safeguards required for personal data. One thing lowers the severity but does not make this a false positive: with a wildcard origin, browsers won't send cookies or other credentials. The risk is greatest for unauthenticated endpoints and for clients that attach tokens manually.
